problem: Current architecture documentation exposed both State Schema v2 and superseded TurnGoalPlan/WorkflowPlan records as plausible authorities, while Python dependency graphs were not locked into release-visible project-local uv.lock files.

options.name: Clarify existing documents only
options.correctness: Reduces wording ambiguity but leaves dependency resolution non-reproducible and permits clean installs to drift from the certified graph.
options.migration: Mark old records as historical and add a current entry document without generating lock files.

options.name: One current architecture authority plus release-visible locks
options.correctness: Makes the State Schema v2 authority chain explicit, retains old records only as superseded history, and binds installations to the dependency graph verified by the product suite.
options.complexity: Bounded to documentation, generated locks, and architecture contract tests; no runtime authority changes.
options.migration: Add CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE, mark obsolete records SUPERSEDED, update references, generate both uv.lock files, and verify clean-release visibility.
options.rollback: Restore the B0 closed baseline documents and remove the two generated lock files; runtime remains unchanged.
options.verification: Expected-red transition, lock freshness checks, full Quick, authenticated HTTP lifecycle, and real Chromium product journey.

options.name: Redesign runtime authority and dependency management together
options.correctness: Could remove more legacy concepts but mixes documentation/reproducibility work with runtime and dependency-cycle redesign, increasing regression and authority-split risk.
options.migration: Replace runtime state/planning structures, dependency assembly, documentation, and installation workflow in one cutover.
options.rollback: Requires reverting runtime checkpoints, documentation, and dependency graph together.
options.verification: New migration suite, checkpoint compatibility, full runtime certification, and real-model evaluation.

rejected_reasons.conservative-doc-only: It leaves dependency resolution non-reproducible and does not satisfy the lock/release claim.
rejected_reasons.redesign-runtime-and-governance: It crosses product-runtime and architecture-governance boundaries and would invalidate the already certified B0 behavior for no necessary A2 benefit.

unknowns: The existing agent_core dependency SCC remains open architecture debt and is explicitly outside A2.
Real DeepSeek semantic behavior remains NOT_DECLARED and requires a later certification target.
selected_responsibilities: CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE.md owns the sole current State Schema v2 architecture description.
Superseded TurnGoalPlan and WorkflowPlan documents remain migration history and cannot own runtime behavior.
Each Python service owns a project-local uv.lock generated from its current pyproject.
Clean-release source selection must include both lock files.
preserved_hard_invariants: Business Service remains the authority for business facts and final writes.
A2 does not claim dependency-cycle closure or real-model certification.
No runtime source is modified by A2.
cutover_strategy: Introduce the current architecture entry and lock files in one documentation/reproducibility candidate, verify the expected-red to green transition, run the full product Quick, then formally close without promoting or changing the architecture baseline policy.
acceptance_claims: The State Schema v2 authority chain is the only current architecture owner and obsolete records are explicitly superseded.
Agent and Business uv.lock files are current, pass uv lock --check, and are included in clean-release source selection.
All required product Gates remain green while architecture debt remains honestly reported as PASS_WITH_DEBT / UNCHANGED.
